page.overview:
What is If You've Got Trouble?

19 March 1996 (US)|recorded=18 February 1965|genre=Rock|length=2:49|row6=Apple Records|songwriter=John Lennon and Paul McCartney|producer=George Martin}}

If You've Got Trouble is a song written by John Lennon and attributed to the Lennon-McCartney partnership. It was recorded by the Beatles on 18 February 1965 with Ringo Starr on lead vocals. Intended for inclusion on the album Help! as Starr's vocal spot, the band later replaced it with a cover of "Act Naturally". It was eventually released on Anthology 2 in 1996, after which it received a mostly negative critical reception.

Following an afternoon recording session from 3.30 pm to 5.15 pm that produced "You've Got to Hide Your Love Away", the Beatles returned to Studio Two at EMI Studios at 6.00 pm to record "If You've Got Trouble", which had been written specifically for Starr. Nonetheless, only one take was performed, with no false starts, before it was deemed "best" and the band moved on to recording "Tell Me What You See".

The song was subject to overdubs, with Starr's vocal being double-tracked and additional guitar work by George Harrison, before a mono mix was produced on 20 February.
